"'''Earned It'''", alternatively titled "'''Earned It (Fifty Shades of Grey)'''",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://play.spotify.com/track/2PIvq1pGrUjY007X5y1UpM|title=Earned It (Fifty Shades Of Grey) – From The "Fifty Shades Of Grey" Soundtrack – The Weeknd|date=2015|publisher=Spotify|access-date=May 11, 2015}}</ref> is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [[the Weeknd]]. The song was released as the lead single from the [[Fifty Shades of Grey (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] to the 2015 film ''[[Fifty Shades of Grey (film)|Fifty Shades of Grey]]'' and was included on the Weeknd's second studio album ''[[Beauty Behind the Madness]]'' (2015).

Unlike the film, which was critically panned, "Earned It" was lauded by critics upon release, and peaked at number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming the Weeknd's first top five single. The song's popularity earned the soundtrack to ''Fifty Shades of Grey'' two concurrent top-ten singles, with [[Ellie Goulding]]'s "[[Love Me like You Do]]" also peaking at number three. Its music video was directed by the film's director, [[Sam Taylor-Johnson]], features the film's lead actress, [[Dakota Johnson]], and has the same [[BDSM]] theme. The song was nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] at the [[88th Academy Awards]] and won the [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance]] at the [[58th Annual Grammy Awards]]. On February 16, 2023, it was certified diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for selling more than ten million copies in the United States.

"Earned It", alternatively titled "Earned It (Fifty Shades of Grey)", is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter the Weeknd. The song was released as the lead single from the soundtrack to the 2015 film Fifty Shades of Grey and was included on the Weeknd's second studio album Beauty Behind the Madness (2015).

Unlike the film, which was critically panned, "Earned It" was lauded by critics upon release, and peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the Weeknd's first top five single. The song's popularity earned the soundtrack to Fifty Shades of Grey two concurrent top-ten singles, with Ellie Goulding's "Love Me like You Do" also peaking at number three. Its music video was directed by the film's director, Sam Taylor-Johnson, features the film's lead actress, Dakota Johnson, and has the same BDSM theme. The song was nominated for Best Original Song at the 88th Academy Awards and won the Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance at the 58th Annual Grammy Awards. On February 16, 2023, it was certified diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for selling more than ten million copies in the United States.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: The Weeknd was involved in the project very early on. Tom Mackay, a manager at Republic Records, explained: "He worked on a number of songs for a number of scenes. Some were working and some weren't, but he just kept at it, and kept at it, and kept at it. In the end, he wrote 'Earned It' and it's the biggest song of his career to date. It's the only song that's in the movie twice".<ref>{{cite web|last1=Ugwu|first1=Reggie|title=Why The "Fifty Shades Of Grey" Soundtrack Is Better Than It Has Any Right To Be|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/reggieugwu/how-the-fifty-shades-of-grey-soundtrack-got-so-good|website=BuzzFeed|access-date=February 27, 2015|date=February 26, 2015}}</ref> Director Sam Taylor-Johnson said the Weeknd's voice is instantly seductive, which fit the film perfectly. The singer agreed saying the film and his music is like "a match made in heaven".<ref name="youtube1">{{cite web|author1=Republic Records|title=Behind the Scenes – The Weeknd "Earned It" (Fifty Shades Of Grey) Video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0bX8xq16PtI|website=YouTube|access-date=June 23, 2015|date=January 21, 2015}}</ref> An alternative version of the single, with a new slightly long intro, was later included in the Weeknd's album ''[[Beauty Behind the Madness]]'' (2015).
sections.text: The Weeknd was involved in the project very early on. Tom Mackay, a manager at Republic Records, explained: "He worked on a number of songs for a number of scenes. Some were working and some weren't, but he just kept at it, and kept at it, and kept at it. In the end, he wrote 'Earned It' and it's the biggest song of his career to date. It's the only song that's in the movie twice". Director Sam Taylor-Johnson said the Weeknd's voice is instantly seductive, which fit the film perfectly. The singer agreed saying the film and his music is like "a match made in heaven". An alternative version of the single, with a new slightly long intro, was later included in the Weeknd's album Beauty Behind the Madness (2015).

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Earned It" is a [[chamber pop]] and [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] song.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.axs.com/news/sam-smith-the-weeknd-and-lady-gaga-nominated-for-academy-awards-74027 | title=Sam Smith, The Weeknd, and Lady Gaga nominated for Academy Awards | publisher=[[AXS TV]] | date=January 16, 2016 | access-date=February 19, 2016 | author=Pankey, William}}</ref> It is written in the key of [[D minor]] with a slow [[tempo]] of 40 beats per minute (Largo) in [[Time signature|{{music|time|6|8}} time]]. There is an alternation between the chords Gm{{small|7}} and Dm{{small|7}}, and Tesfaye's vocals span two octaves from D<sub>3</sub> to D<sub>5</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Earned It (Fifty Shades of Grey)|url = http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0147888|website = www.musicnotes.com|date = March 13, 2015|access-date = January 14, 2016}}</ref>

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Critics praised "Earned It" upon release, with Mitchell Bozzetto of ''[[Renowned for Sound]]'' writing, "Tesfaye definitely has one of the best modern day R&B voices and it certainly shows in this track, his pitch and tone are spot on which makes this a soothing listen."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://renownedforsound.com/single-review-the-weeknd-earned-it-fifty-shades-of-grey/|title=Single Review: The Weeknd – 'Earned It' (Fifty Shades Of Grey)|date=January 26, 2015 |publisher=[[Renowned for Sound]]|access-date=April 1, 2023}}</ref> Tom Breihan of ''[[Stereogum]]'' wrote, "With its streaking, soundtracky strings, "Earned It" almost sounds like it could come from one of the '80s erotic thrillers that clearly inspired ''Fifty Shades''. It's not a great Weeknd song, but it's a pretty interesting career move.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/1726316/the-weeknd-earned-it/news/|title=The Weeknd – "Earned It"|date=December 23, 2014 |publisher=[[Stereogum]]|access-date=April 1, 2023}}</ref>

Andrew Ryce of ''[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]'' praised the Weeknd's vocals but said that the song is "kind of icky".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/20999-beauty-behind-the-madness/|title=Beauty Behind the Madness|publisher=Pitchfork|access-date=April 4, 2023}}</ref> [[Kitty Empire]] of ''[[The Guardian]]'' called the song "a genre curveball that nevertheless sat comfortably with the Weeknd's depraved brand identity, cultivated over [[Trilogy (The Weeknd album)|three mixtapes]]."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2015/aug/30/the-weeknd-beauty-behind-madness-review|title=The Weeknd: Beauty Behind the Madness review – a dark seduction of the mainstream|work=The Guardian|date=August 30, 2015 |access-date=April 4, 2023 |last1=Empire |first1=Kitty }}</ref>

''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked the song at number 39 on its "50 best songs of 2015" list: "The [[Fifty Shades of Grey (soundtrack)|50 Shades of Grey soundtrack]] proved Abel Tesfaye's ideal entree into the pop mainstream, though here he eschewed [[S&M]] to instead focus on the bottom line, lending his liquid falsetto to the role of affectionate sugar daddy."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/50-best-songs-of-2015-144910/|title=50 Best Songs of 2015|date=December 3, 2015|publisher=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=April 1, 2023}}</ref>

Tom Breihan of Stereogum wrote, "With its streaking, soundtracky strings, "Earned It" almost sounds like it could come from one of the '80s erotic thrillers that clearly inspired Fifty Shades. It's not a great Weeknd song, but it's a pretty interesting career move.

sections.heading: Accolades
sections.wikitext:
The song won the [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance]] at the [[58th Annual Grammy Awards]], while also being nominated for [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Song|Best R&B Song]], and [[Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media|Best Song Written for Visual Media]].<ref>https://www.nytimes.com/2015/12/0t8/arts/music/grammy-awards-kendrick-lamar-taylor-swift-and-the-weeknd-lead-nominations.html {{dead link|date=September 2021}}</ref> The song also received a nomination for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] at the [[88th Academy Awards]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/oscars-2016-weeknd-sam-smith-lady-gaga-lead-song-nominations-20160114|title=The Weeknd, Sam Smith, Lady Gaga Lead Best Song Oscar Noms – Rolling Stone|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=January 14, 2016|access-date=August 26, 2017|archive-date=January 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116024311/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/oscars-2016-weeknd-sam-smith-lady-gaga-lead-song-nominations-20160114|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The song won the Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance at the 58th Annual Grammy Awards, while also being nominated for Best R&B Song, and Best Song Written for Visual Media. The song also received a nomination for Best Original Song at the 88th Academy Awards.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
In the Weeknd's native Canada, "Earned It" peaked at number eight on the [[Canadian Hot 100]]. "Earned It" peaked at number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], the second single from the ''[[Fifty Shades of Grey (soundtrack)|Fifty Shades of Grey soundtrack]]'' to enter the top 10, after [[Ellie Goulding]]{{'}}s "[[Love Me like You Do]]", which also peaked at number three. It became the Weeknd's second top-ten hit, after his collaboration with [[Ariana Grande]] on the number seven peaking hit, "[[Love Me Harder]]" and his highest-selling song on the chart at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/6480602/mark-ronson-bruno-mars-top-hot-100-again-the-weeknd-enters-top-10|title=Mark Ronson & Bruno Mars Top Hot 100 Again; The Weeknd Enters Top 10|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=February 25, 2015|access-date=March 3, 2015|publisher=Billboard|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825075354/https://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/6480602/mark-ronson-bruno-mars-top-hot-100-again-the-weeknd-enters-top-10|archive-date=August 25, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The song has also been a commercial success overseas, reaching the top ten in 10 other countries, including the United Kingdom, Sweden, Denmark, Switzerland, Spain, Norway and New Zealand, while attaining a top twenty position in countries that include Australia, Germany, and Ireland.
In France, the song debuted at number 162 by the end of January 2015, becoming the Weeknd's second entry in the country after "Love Me Harder" with [[Ariana Grande]]. The following week, the song jumped at number 38, becoming his second top forty. Three weeks later, it reached the top five, peaking at number 2, blocked by "[[Uptown Funk]]" by [[Bruno Mars]] and Mark Ranson, and becoming the Weeknd's highest-charting song at the time, before being surpassed by "[[Starboy (song)|Starboy]]" (2016) with Daft Punk next year, which topped the [[Syndicat National de l'Edition Phonographique|French Singles Chart]]. The song was later certified gold by the [[Syndicat National de l'Edition Phonographique|SNEP]] for over 75,000 units sold.

In the Weeknd's native Canada, "Earned It" peaked at number eight on the Canadian Hot 100. "Earned It" peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot 100, the second single from the Fifty Shades of Grey soundtrack to enter the top 10, after Ellie Goulding{{'}}s "Love Me like You Do", which also peaked at number three. It became the Weeknd's second top-ten hit, after his collaboration with Ariana Grande on the number seven peaking hit, "Love Me Harder" and his highest-selling song on the chart at the time. The song has also been a commercial success overseas, reaching the top ten in 10 other countries, including the United Kingdom, Sweden, Denmark, Switzerland, Spain, Norway and New Zealand, while attaining a top twenty position in countries that include Australia, Germany, and Ireland.
In France, the song debuted at number 162 by the end of January 2015, becoming the Weeknd's second entry in the country after "Love Me Harder" with Ariana Grande. The following week, the song jumped at number 38, becoming his second top forty. Three weeks later, it reached the top five, peaking at number 2, blocked by "Uptown Funk" by Bruno Mars and Mark Ranson, and becoming the Weeknd's highest-charting song at the time, before being surpassed by "Starboy" (2016) with Daft Punk next year, which topped the French Singles Chart. The song was later certified gold by the SNEP for over 75,000 units sold.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video, directed by the film's director [[Sam Taylor-Johnson]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.etonline.com/music/156614_fifty_shades_dakota_johnson_is_all_tied_up_the_weeknd_earned_it_music_video/|title='Fifty Shades': Dakota Johnson Gets Tied Up in The Weeknd's 'Earned It' Music Video|last=Schilliac|first=Sophia|date=January 21, 2015|access-date=January 25, 2015|publisher=ETOnline}}</ref> was shot at the [[Broadway Theater District (Los Angeles)|Palace Theater]] in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Bacardi|first1=Francesca|title=The Weeknd Debuts a Sexy Sneak Peek Video for Fifty Shades of Grey Song "Earned It"—Watch Now!|url=http://uk.eonline.com/news/616543/the-weeknd-debuts-a-sexy-sneak-peek-video-for-fifty-shades-of-grey-song-earned-it-watch-now|website=E! Online|access-date=June 23, 2015|date=January 20, 2015}}</ref> It was released on [[Vevo]] and [[YouTube]] on January 21, 2015. It includes the [[BDSM]] theme as seen in the film. The video shows The Weeknd performing on stage as a group of topless women with black tape over their breasts perform a BDSM-themed burlesque routine behind him. Dakota Johnson makes a cameo appearance in the video.
sections.text: The music video, directed by the film's director Sam Taylor-Johnson, was shot at the Palace Theater in Los Angeles. It was released on Vevo and YouTube on January 21, 2015. It includes the BDSM theme as seen in the film. The video shows The Weeknd performing on stage as a group of topless women with black tape over their breasts perform a BDSM-themed burlesque routine behind him. Dakota Johnson makes a cameo appearance in the video.
